scope: Bounded location investigation, not a systematic literature review or new orbital-data inversion. External copies stay on the research drive; this repository contains source metadata and concise factual annotations.

sources.title: LROC Pits Atlas: Marius Hills Pit
sources.access: Full catalogue page read. Coordinates, inner opening 49–55 m, listed depth 40 m, boulders and uncertain deeper access.

sources.title: LROC Pits Atlas: Mare Tranquillitatis Pit
sources.access: Full catalogue page read. Coordinates, inner opening 88–100 m, 105 m inner depth below a roughly 20 m funnel, visible overhangs.

sources.title: LROC Pits Atlas: Mare Ingenii Pit
sources.access: Full catalogue page read. Coordinates, 71–104 m inner opening and overhangs of at least 10–20 m.

sources.title: LROC Pits Atlas: Lacus Mortis Pit
sources.access: Full catalogue page read. Coordinates, access slope, north-wall overhang with apparent back wall; depth fields have a funnel reference.

sources.title: LROC Pits Atlas: Schlüter Pit
sources.access: Full catalogue page read. Highland classification, coordinates and small opening with overhang near a mare patch.

sources.title: Kaku et al. (2017), Detection of Intact Lava Tubes at Marius Hills on the Moon by SELENE (Kaguya) Lunar Radar Sounder
sources.access: Main text read through publisher HTML: abstract, methods, results, discussion and conclusion. More than 80 candidate echo locations, interpretation alternatives and the radar/gravity comparison; the conclusion interprets these as an intact tube. No surveyed continuous 30 km usable interior is admitted.

sources.title: Chappaz et al. (2017), Evidence of large empty lava tubes on the Moon using GRAIL gravity
sources.access: Publisher abstract, method sections and results/Table 1 read. The Schröter extension model is an inversion, not measured cavity dimensions. Table 1 places the anomaly approximately at 24 N, 306 E. Supporting-information parameter grids were not reanalysed.

sources.title: Kaku et al. (2018), Existence of a lunar lava tube at west of Rima Mairan suggested by SELENE LRS, LPSC abstract 1830
sources.access: Both pages read. Point P0 at 35.892 N, 313.235 E and nearby radar echoes coincide with a gravity deficit; the paper allows a subsurface layer or wide cave. Conference evidence, no interior survey.

sources.title: NASA (18 July 2024), New Evidence Adds to Findings Hinting at Network of Caves on Moon
sources.access: Article body read. Mission report of the Carrer result: cave evidence extending more than 200 feet from the pit, with total extent unknown. No secondary width/depth values transferred.

sources.title: Carrer et al. (2024), Radar evidence of an accessible cave conduit on the Moon below the Mare Tranquillitatis pit
sources.access: Publisher search record and abstract/caption context only in this investigation. Publisher HTML and PDF retrieval failed through the identity redirect; Trento repository retrieval returned 403. Full source remains unretrieved. The limited cave-extension claim uses the separately identified NASA mission report; no detailed numerical geometry is admitted from unread text.

sources.title: Le Corre et al. (2025), New candidate cave entrances on the Moon found using deep learning, Icarus 441, 116675
sources.access: Repository publisher PDF, introduction and sections 4.2–4.3 and conclusion context read. Coordinates and interpretation of South Marius Hills and Belkovich A; the 1.92% maria survey adds entrances, not confirmed large connected cave volumes. Detector confidence is not a city-suitability probability.

sources.title: NASA (30 September 2026, corrected 2 October), NASA Adds New Science Investigations for Moon Base
sources.access: Release body read. GIMLI selected to investigate whether Marius Hills Pit opens into a large lava tube. Selection is not a completed survey or delivery forecast.

sources.title: Planetary Science Institute (1 October 2026), PSI-led team selected for NASA PRISM program to explore potential lunar cave
sources.access: Article body read. Proposed ground-penetrating radar, seismic, gravity and camera investigations would test the existence and size of a void.

sources.title: Mittelholz et al. (2026), Lava Tube Exploration with LunarLeaper, Advances in Geophysics 67
sources.access: Abstract and introduction read in arXiv v1 HTML. Formation and pit-type context; a mission concept for in-situ investigation. The full 49-page instrument/performance study was not reviewed.
